claim: For every \(0\leq\chi\leq\pi/4\), let \(U_\chi=\exp[-i(\frac{\pi}{4}X\otimes X+\chi Y\otimes Y)]\), and let \(R_y(\pi/2)=\exp(-i\pi Y/4)\). For the two-qubit maximally entangled mixed state \(\rho_{\rm ME}(\gamma,-\pi/2)\) with \(0\leq\gamma\leq1\), the state \(\sigma_{\gamma,\chi}=U_\chi^\dagger(R_y(\pi/2)\otimes I)\rho_{\rm ME}(\gamma,-\pi/2)(R_y(-\pi/2)\otimes I)U_\chi\) is separable for every \(\gamma\). More precisely, for the rank-three branch \(0\leq\gamma\leq2/3\), the spectrum of \(\sigma_{\gamma,\chi}^{T_B}\) is exactly \(\{0,1/3,1/3-\gamma/2,1/3+\gamma/2\}\), independent of \(\chi\); for the rank-two branch \(2/3\leq\gamma\leq1\), it is \(\{0,0,1-\gamma,\gamma\}\). Hence the fixed local rotation supplies a separable source whose image under \(U_\chi\) is a local-unitary copy of a MEMS at every purity \(1/3\leq\mu\leq1\), giving an analytic all-purity certificate for the \(U_c(\pi/4,\chi,0)\) family that Guan et al. reported from a numerical local-rotation scan. The rank-two existence portion is already implied by Di and Liu's 2007 theorem for pure-state perfect entanglers; the new substantive step is the exact rank-three certificate and its single fixed rotation.
integrity: The infinite parameter statement is proved by exact symbolic characteristic-polynomial identities plus the two-qubit PPT-separability theorem; finite numerical sampling is not used as proof. The rank-two portion is explicitly credited to prior broader coverage where applicable.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is for the canonical family U_c(pi/4,chi,0), two-qubit MEMS, and 0<=chi<=pi/4. It does not classify all global perfect entanglers or the broader rank-three regions seen numerically, and it does not claim novelty for rank-two existence.
title: A fixed-rotation analytic proof for the second global mixed-state perfect-entangler family
